string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of China.Located in northern China, it is an important centre for politics, culture, international exchanges, and scientific innovation. Its urban history stretches back more than three thousand years. The city served as a capital during several dynasties, including the Yuan, Ming, and Qing. Mountains surround much of its northern and western territory, while plains extend towards the southeast. Today, Beijing combines its long historical identity with the responsibilities and activities of a modern national capital.

Shanghai is one of the biggest city in the east China and is important centre for international finance and trade. The Huangpu River is a major feature of its urban landscape, connecting different parts of the city and shaping its waterfront. Along the Bund, historic buildings reflect the development of financial institutions and trading companies. Across the river, Pudong represents a more recent period of urban and economic growth. Shanghai also preserves traditional neighbourhoods, gardens, and cultural attractions. The combination of historic streets, busy commercial districts, and modern buildings gives the city a distinctive character.

Chongqing is a municipality in southwestern China, situated along the upper reaches of the Yangtze River. Its central urban area developed around the meeting point of the Yangtze and Jialing rivers. The surrounding mountains and river valleys strongly influence the layout of the city, giving it a distinctive landscape. Beyond the central districts, the municipality includes other urban centres and extensive mountainous areas. The Yangtze connects many of these places and passes through the famous Three Gorges region. Chongqing also serves as an important regional centre for transport, commerce, finance, and administration.

Tianjin is a municipality in northern China near Beijing and the Bohai Sea. The Haihe River runs through the city and has played an important role in its development. Historically, waterways helped Tianjin become a centre for transporting grain and other goods. A military garrison established in 1404 marked an important stage in the history of the city. Tianjin later developed into a major commercial and industrial centre. Today, its seaport connects northern China with international shipping networks. Its riverfront and historic districts also reflect a long history of trade and cultural exchange.
